primitives.name: UX Ten-Second Comprehension Layer
primitives.verbatim_quote: Your job is to make the product feel inevitable: the clearest, most premium, most trustworthy NFL intelligence experience on the internet.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{comprehension}': 'Time to comprehend core data story (seconds)', 'H_{structure}': 'Hierarchical information architecture depth', 'E_{explanation}': 'Explanatory clarity of metrics', 'S_{storytelling}': 'Narrative cohesion of data confidence', 'N_{metrics}': 'Total number of metrics displayed'}

The Data Coverage Deficit (C_{deficit}) is the foundational constraint that drives the need for the UX Ten-Second Comprehension Layer (T_{comprehension}). If coverage is insufficient, users cannot rapidly understand the data landscape, leading to suboptimal decisions. The Licensed Data Scaffold (L_{scaffold}) is the operational mechanism that feeds into reducing C_{deficit}. Finally, the King Standard Scorecard (K_{scorecard}) provides a unified evaluation metric that retroactively validates whether the entire system meets regulatory and performance standards. This creates a closed-loop system where each primitive addresses a specific failure mode: scarcity, comprehension, acquisition, and validation.
